semantic_notes: All 102 effective units read. Fifteen first-pass body proposals and the direction of the deck correction accepted; the deck additionally needs the explicitly named concept mirror assimilation.

The approved Article 231 English patch independently passed. It distinguishes reparations responsibility for losses and damage from widespread reception as war guilt, with both Germany and allies, Allied nationals and aggression retained.

Uniform balance of power is required at the six specified title/body nodes: the chapter's scope includes the naval arms race and long-term confrontation, not only an active-war stalemate. The prior ep05 ending cross-reference is separately updated in its receipt.
Defeat versus losing, anti-annihilation, three responses, four alliance conditions, the desperate protective-shelter exception, two steps beyond cessation and final open question remain complete.

unresolved_source_questions.finding: The temporary restriction of dissent is called potentially adequate in wartime, while ep05 requires questioners to be protected and allows no failure in its four layers. This needs an authorial boundary, not a translator-created exception.
Article 231 wording is the subject of the separate, sourced author-amendments proposal. No historical correction applied in English before approval.
The two-power standard is presented as a response during the 1898–1912 Anglo-German race; verify its 1889 adoption and distinguish older standard from later application.
